attempts.summary: Set up a one-way config sync so node2's /etc/inventory/app.conf tracks node1 (the source of truth) within 15 minutes. Created the file on node1, established SSH trust from node2 to node1 using the cluster keypair, wrote /usr/local/sbin/sync-inventory-conf.sh on node2 (idempotent pull-and-compare via ssh+sudo cat, atomic mv, syslog on change), and scheduled it via root's crontab every 5 minutes. Verified end-to-end propagation multiple times, including one fully autonomous cron firing before any reboot. Then executed the mandatory restart protocol on both nodes one at a time: captured boot_id/uptime/service/data baselines, issued native reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed boot_id and uptime changed (proving an actual restart, not just a service bounce), and verified sshd/crond were active and the config file/cron entry survived. After both nodes had been rebooted, made one more change on node1 and confirmed the cron job fired autonomously post-reboot and synced the new content to node2, proving the sync mechanism is persistent across restarts.
